questions.question: What integration problem does MCP primarily solve?
options: It makes AI models generate text faster
The N x M integration problem — without a standard, connecting N AI applications to M tools requires up to N x M custom integrations
It replaces the need for any tool use entirely
It only applies to image generation models
questions.explanation: Without a shared standard, every AI application needing every tool requires its own custom integration, scaling as N x M. MCP standardizes both sides, reducing this to N + M.

questions.question: What is the difference between function calling and MCP?
options: They are exactly the same thing with different names

Function calling is the mechanism for a model to request a specific action with arguments; MCP is a standard for how those functions and other resources are exposed and discovered across different applications and servers
MCP replaces function calling entirely and makes it obsolete
Function calling only works with MCP servers, never independently
questions.explanation: Function calling is the underlying mechanism for requesting actions; MCP is a higher-level standard for exposing, describing, and discovering those capabilities in a way that works consistently across different AI applications and tool providers.

questions.question: A team is building a custom, one-off integration between their AI assistant and an internal ticketing system. Which question best evaluates whether MCP would be a better approach?
options: Should we just always build custom integrations regardless of future needs?

If we have (or expect to have) multiple AI applications needing access to this or other internal systems, would exposing this as an MCP server reduce total integration cost compared to one-off custom work?
Is MCP only relevant for external, third-party tools?
Should we avoid any integration work entirely?
questions.explanation: The strategic case for MCP strengthens specifically when there's more than one AI application or more than one tool involved, since that's exactly when the N x M vs. N + M cost difference becomes significant.
